spec_match.rationale: Reads a genuinely paced same-origin stream (/public/slow-stream server route) chunk by chunk and aborts mid-stream with four structured Error reasons, routing on error.cause at the reader — the exact stream-forwarding contract Chrome 154 adds.

interactive.rationale: Start plus four cause buttons with a live progress track, chunk/byte readouts, a routing panel and a timestamped log; verified a real cancellation at 26 chunks mid-stream.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises a chunked download ended for four causes and routed on the reason, which is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Download-finished-before-abort, fetch-rejecting-before-body, and the pre-154 no-cause state each have distinct honest handling, and the server pacing rationale is documented in the note.

conformance.rationale: The suite's body-stream-rejects-with-the-reason assertion is this page's contract; on Chromium 141 /conformance/ reported 5 pass / 2 fail with that assertion honestly failing pre-154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): started the download, progress advanced (26 chunks), clicked User cancelled — reader rejected with a bare AbortError, 'reason reached the reader: no', and the detail correctly explained the four-causes-collapse pre-154; console clean, the ERR_ABORTED entries are the intentional aborts.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a stream-cancelled assert with cause/chunks/bytes/reached.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, secondary buttons override background and color together, progress bar carries a text readout, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: The log is an aria-live labelled list, the readout uses dl semantics, the progress track has a text overlay, and all buttons are labelled with 44px targets.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); the button row and readout grid wrap.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/fetch-api-forward-reason-from-abortcontroller-to-fetch-response/streaming-download/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). This is a model concept page: a real server-paced stream (262144 bytes in 8KB chunks with 60ms delays) gives an actual mid-stream to cancel in, the four cause buttons abort the same controller with structured reasons, and on this pre-154 build the page honestly reported that the reader got a bare AbortError with no cause, exactly the gap the feature closes. Live progress, routing panel, log, clean console (ERR_ABORTED entries are the demo's own aborts), no mobile overflow. /conformance/ reported 5 pass / 2 fail, the fails being the two Chrome-154 forwarding assertions. No follow-ups.
